profile.name: Khairunnisa Fajriyanti
profile.intro: I enjoy understanding how systems behave, turning requirements into test scenarios, documenting findings clearly, and exploring how software quality affects real users and workflows.
profile.about: I am an Informatics Engineering graduate (GPA 3.49/4.00) with experience in manual testing, UAT, regression testing, test case design, defect documentation, application administration, data validation, and technical writing. I have worked across enterprise and web applications with different levels of documentation and development maturity. I enjoy breaking down workflows, identifying edge cases, clarifying expected behavior, and communicating findings in a way that helps teams decide what to do next.
profile.education: Bachelor's Degree in Informatics Engineering — UHAMKA | GPA 3.49 / 4.00
profile.certification: Mini Bootcamp Software Testing — PT Bajau Escorindo (2025)
profile.footerText: Open to learning, collaboration, and early-career QA opportunities.

projects.title: CCTV & AI Security
projects.subtitle: Edge-case testing and requirement clarification
projects.summary: Manual QA exposure on a web-based perimeter-security platform integrating CCTV monitoring and AI-powered features. Internal product details and screenshots are intentionally omitted.
projects.role: Observed and tested available application behavior, developed test scenarios and user documentation, and communicated findings for clarification.
projects.challenge: The application was partially developed when testing began, while detailed product documentation and requirements were initially limited.
approach: Explored available features and user flows.
Compared observed behavior with the information available and recorded observations.
Raised questions where expected behavior or classification rules needed clarification.
projects.finding: A registered visitor's name appeared when the face was almost fully visible. When the face was partially visible at an angle, the system displayed “Stranger”.
projects.outcome: Documented the observation and identified questions for expected behavior. Follow-up implementation status is unknown.
projects.learning: Learned to separate observed behavior from a confirmed defect, and to clarify recognition rules before defining expected results. This work validated application-visible behavior, not AI model performance.

projects.title: Internal ERP / HRIS
projects.subtitle: Workflow quality and data-integrity risks
projects.summary: Manual testing and user feedback for an internal enterprise system supporting employee processes and asset requests.
projects.role: Reviewed user workflows, identified issues, documented observations, collected user feedback, and communicated findings and improvement ideas to relevant stakeholders.
projects.challenge: An overtime-request workflow could lead users to submit a second request when actual overtime differed from the estimate, while the form did not offer an edit option.
approach: Followed the workflow that led to duplicate submissions.
Documented the potential impact on overtime records and calculations.
Discussed a possible workflow alternative with HR.
projects.finding: The design created a risk of duplicate overtime records or calculations when the original request could not be edited.
projects.outcome: Shared the finding and a proposed alternative. The implementation outcome was not confirmed.
projects.learning: Learned to connect user behavior, workflow design, data integrity, and operational impact when analyzing quality issues.

projects.title: Drone Ground Control Station
projects.subtitle: System discovery and test planning
projects.summary: Early-stage exploration of a Ground Control Station (GCS) application while the system was still under development.
projects.role: Reviewed available UI and feature walkthroughs, outlined workflows, and drafted initial test scenarios based on the information available.
projects.challenge: The system was still being developed and access to a test/staging environment was limited.
approach: Reviewed available screens and feature walkthroughs.
Translated verbally explained workflows into an initial test-flow outline.
Drafted candidate test scenarios and documented access limitations.
projects.finding: Several behaviors required validation in an accessible test environment; drafted scenarios were not equivalent to executed tests.
projects.outcome: Prepared initial test-planning documentation. Comprehensive test execution was not performed.
projects.learning: Learned to distinguish discovery and test design from test execution, and to document environment/access blockers.
